# Configure the AI Inference Gateway

This page describes how to configure the [AI Inference Gateway](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/model-access) on Kubernetes. You register model services, define an inference pool, and deploy a gateway that routes agent requests to those models.

@include '../../../global/partials/alerts/beta.mdx'

@include 'alerts/enterprise-alert.mdx'

## Background

An AI Inference Gateway on Kubernetes uses three kinds of objects:

| Object | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| Model services | Pods annotated with `consul.hashicorp.com/ai-role: inference-model`. Consul registers them as model upstreams that gateways discover in the catalog. |
| [`InferencePoolConfig`](/consul/docs/reference/k8s/ai/inferencepoolconfig) | Defines the gateway's processor, failover, PII, and telemetry settings. |
| [`InferenceGateway`](/consul/docs/reference/k8s/ai/inferencegateway) | Deploys the gateway. It references one `InferencePoolConfig`. |

For each `InferenceGateway`, the controller creates a Deployment, a Service, and an [`inference-gateway` configuration entry](/consul/docs/reference/config-entry/inference-gateway) from the referenced pool.

## Requirements

- Consul Agentic Runtime Fabric installed with `ai.enabled` and `ai.inferenceGateway.enabled` set to `true`. Refer to [Install Consul Agentic Runtime Fabric](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/install).

## Register model services

Annotate the pod template of each model service. The gateway discovers models from these registrations.

<CodeBlockConfig highlight="4-9">

```yaml
template:
  metadata:
    annotations:
      consul.hashicorp.com/connect-inject: "true"
      consul.hashicorp.com/ai-role: inference-model
      consul.hashicorp.com/ai-inference-model-protocol: openai
      consul.hashicorp.com/ai-inference-model-path: /v1
      consul.hashicorp.com/service-meta-capabilities: "chat,summarize"
      consul.hashicorp.com/service-meta-priority_chat: "0"
```

</CodeBlockConfig>

The annotations set the following values:

- `consul.hashicorp.com/ai-inference-model-protocol`: The API dialect the model serves. Set `openai`, `anthropic`, or `passthrough`. Defaults to `openai`.
- `consul.hashicorp.com/ai-inference-model-path`: The base path of the model API. Defaults to `/v1`.
- `consul.hashicorp.com/service-meta-capabilities`: A comma-separated list of the capabilities the model serves.
- `consul.hashicorp.com/service-meta-priority_<capability>`: The model's rank for one capability. Lower values have higher priority, and `0` is the primary tier. Models with the same rank share a tier and are load balanced. A model without a rank sorts last. Because the rank is per capability, one model can be primary for one capability and a backup for another.

You can also set `consul.hashicorp.com/service-meta-model_family` to name the concrete upstream model. The gateway applies it to a request whose model is `auto`.

## Define the inference pool

Create an `InferencePoolConfig` that attaches to the gateway with `parentRefs`. The following example fails over across up to two tiers, masks email addresses in requests and responses, and exports traces.

<CodeBlockConfig filename="inference-pool.yaml">

```yaml
apiVersion: consul.hashicorp.com/v1alpha1
kind: InferencePoolConfig
metadata:
  name: travel-pool
  namespace: default
spec:
  enabled: true
  parentRefs:
    - kind: InferenceGateway
      name: travel-inference
  processor:
    failureMode: closed
  routing:
    fallback:
      retryOn: ["5xx", "connect-failure"]
      maxTiers: 2
      perTryTimeout: 30s
  policy:
    pii:
      scope: both
      defaultAction: mask
      detectors:
        - name: email
  observability:
    tracing:
      enabled: true
      sampleRatio: 1
      otlp:
        endpoint: otel-collector:4318
```

</CodeBlockConfig>

In Consul 2.1, the controller applies only the `processor`, `routing.fallback`, `policy.pii`, and `observability` fields. Refer to the [`InferencePoolConfig` reference](/consul/docs/reference/k8s/ai/inferencepoolconfig) for the fields that have no effect.

## Deploy the gateway

Create an `InferenceGateway` that references the pool.

<CodeBlockConfig filename="inference-gateway.yaml">

```yaml
apiVersion: consul.hashicorp.com/v1alpha1
kind: InferenceGateway
metadata:
  name: travel-inference
  namespace: default
spec:
  poolRef:
    name: travel-pool
```

</CodeBlockConfig>

Apply both resources:

```shell-session
$ kubectl apply --filename inference-pool.yaml --filename inference-gateway.yaml
```

You can also create gateways from Helm with the [`ai.inferenceGateway.gateways`](/consul/docs/reference/k8s/helm#v-ai-inferencegateway-gateways) value. The chart renders one `InferenceGateway` for each entry.

## Authorize traffic

Service intentions decide which agents can call the gateway and which models the gateway can reach. Create intentions that allow each agent to call the gateway service and allow the gateway service to call each model service. Refer to [Service intentions](/consul/docs/reference/config-entry/service-intentions).

## Route requests

Agents send OpenAI-compatible requests to the gateway over their mesh upstream. The gateway routes each request in one of two modes:

- **Capability routing.** The default. The caller sets the `x-inference-specialization` request header to a capability, and the gateway sends the request to the highest-priority tier of models that serve that capability.
- **Body model routing.** Set `processor.bodyModelRouting` to `true` in the pool. The gateway routes on the model named in the request body.
